doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Pharaoh Sanders and the Theresa catalog
title: Sam Lay and Frank Frost blues recordings
summary: Gordon explains he bought the Sam Lay and Frank Frost recordings from the same producer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I was going to ask you, I mean you put out so many great blues re-issues and then some fresh recordings. Your Sam Lay record, was that an original recording?

The Sam Lay recording, a producer/musician, a guy who wanted to have his fun recording, making recordings, you know, made the recording and called the record companies to try and sell it, it’s not uncommon, it’s very common, and so no. I bought that from the producer of the session.
I wondered ‘cause we spoke previously about our mutual love for the Butterfield band and you know his outstanding drumming on the first couple of records there.
Yeah, yeah. I mean that was thrilling.
I’m sure. Frank Frost, the harmonica player?
Oh interesting. Same producer, yeah. Okay. Yeah, great connection there to Sun Records.
Yeah, and a great record, an excellent record.
